column1: # Mutation manifest — id <TAB> kind <TAB> suite <TAB> what its survival would mean
# kind=env  an environment override for the suite only; the platform is not
#           touched, and the question is "would this suite notice?"
# kind=svc  a service is stopped under the suite; the platform IS touched and
#           is restored afterwards, including by the EXIT trap.
# Few and meaningful, not exhaustive (Google's lesson): every row destroys one
# behaviour a suite claims to prove, and the last column is the sentence a

column4: storage passes without a MinIO client: the mc steps report success on a container that was never created
storage passes with the wrong secret key: the suite proves nothing about authentication to MinIO
storage passes with the storage plane stopped
the CORS suite passes from an origin the gateway must refuse: it never read the header it asserts on
a suite is green against a gateway that is not there — the vacuous-pass case that HTTP 000 used to hide
realtime passes with the realtime plane stopped
the Mongo MVP passes with the mongo API stopped
the engine backup gate passes when the restore validates the archive and applies nothing: the data is not back and nobody would know
the offers collection passes with no user identity, as it did while authEmail was seeded empty
the security gate passes with the WAF itself stopped — exactly what it did while it curled a port nothing listens on
